sections.title: What AI contract intelligence can do
sections.description: Extraction, classification, comparison, obligation tracking, and risk flagging across contract portfolios.

content.text: The core capabilities span a spectrum of value. Extraction — pulling structured data from contracts: party names, effective dates, payment terms, termination clauses, liability caps, governing law, renewal dates — converting unstructured contract text into queryable structured records. Classification — identifying contract types and flagging high-risk or non-standard provisions that deviate from standard templates. Comparison — comparing contract terms across a portfolio to identify inconsistencies or negotiation outcomes across counterparties. Obligation tracking — surfacing upcoming deadlines, renewal windows, and obligation milestones from contract provisions. Risk flagging — identifying specific clause types (unlimited liability, broad IP assignment, unusual termination triggers) that warrant attorney review.

items: Extraction — party names, dates, payment terms, termination clauses, liability caps.
Classification — contract types, standard vs. non-standard provisions.
Comparison — identify inconsistencies across the portfolio.
Obligation tracking — deadlines, renewal windows, milestones.
Risk flagging — unusual clauses warranting attorney review.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: AI contract intelligence handles extraction and pattern identification at scale — freeing legal teams to focus on the judgment work.

sections.title: What AI contract intelligence cannot replace

content.text: AI contract intelligence handles extraction, classification, and pattern identification at scale — it does not replace legal judgment. Identifying that a contract contains a non-standard limitation-of-liability clause is extraction; determining whether to accept that clause in this specific business context requires attorney judgment that AI surfaces for but doesn't replace. ClickMasters is direct about this boundary: AI contract intelligence accelerates legal review by handling the volume work, freeing attorneys for the judgment work — not eliminating the attorney from the process.

items: Extraction ≠ judgment — identifying clauses is not the same as evaluating them.
Attorney judgment required — legal interpretation and negotiation remain human.
Volume work — AI handles the scale; attorneys handle the decisions.
Direct boundary — ClickMasters is honest about what AI can and cannot replace.

sections.title: Limitations and risks of AI contract intelligence

content.text: AI contract intelligence has limitations. Extraction accuracy depends on contract complexity and language variability. Legal language is highly variable, and models may misclassify provisions without careful tuning. Contract formats vary widely, and scanned documents require OCR with its own accuracy limits. The system cannot replace legal judgment — it only surfaces information for attorney review. Contract portfolios are dynamic, requiring ongoing updates as new contracts are added. Over-reliance on automated extraction without legal review can create risk.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions about AI contract intelligence

items.question: What contract types does AI contract intelligence handle best?
items.answer: Extraction accuracy is highest for standardized commercial contracts (NDAs, MSAs, SaaS agreements) with consistent structure; more variable or highly negotiated contract types require more training data specific to those formats.

items.question: Can AI contract intelligence handle scanned contracts, not just digital text?
items.answer: Yes, with OCR preprocessing for scanned documents — ClickMasters integrates document digitization as part of the contract intelligence pipeline where needed.

items.question: How does AI contract intelligence handle contracts in multiple languages?
items.answer: Requires multilingual NLP models or separate extraction models per language — ClickMasters scopes multilingual requirements during Discovery and designs accordingly.

items.question: Can the system flag clauses that deviate from our standard templates?
items.answer: Yes — clause comparison against standard templates is a common and valuable contract intelligence capability, identifying deviations that warrant review.

items.question: How long does building a contract intelligence system take?
items.answer: 12–28 weeks depending on contract type diversity and system scope.

items.question: Does AI contract intelligence work for compliance monitoring of existing contract obligations?
items.answer: Yes — obligation and deadline extraction is a high-value capability for ensuring existing contract terms (renewal windows, payment milestones, audit rights) are tracked and acted on.

items.question: What is the difference between contract intelligence and contract lifecycle management?
items.answer: Contract lifecycle management (CLM) is the broader business process for managing contracts from creation to execution. Contract intelligence is the AI-powered extraction and analysis layer that often integrates with CLM systems to enhance their capabilities.

items.question: Can AI contract intelligence handle highly negotiated contracts with non-standard language?
items.answer: Yes, but extraction accuracy may be lower for highly variable, non-standard language. ClickMasters tunes models for your specific contract portfolio and includes human review for low-confidence extractions.

items.question: How do you protect sensitive contract data in AI contract intelligence systems?
items.answer: ClickMasters implements appropriate security controls, data access permissions, and privacy safeguards based on your contract data sensitivity. Processing can be configured on-premises or in your cloud environment.

items.question: What is the role of RAG in AI contract intelligence?
items.answer: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) enables natural language querying over the contract portfolio — allowing users to ask questions like 'which contracts have unlimited liability clauses?' and get grounded answers based on the extracted contract data.
